reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap point in Italy tagged as a data center is almost certainly a small professional office, not compute infrastructure.

The record is named Studio BETA SRLS in Porto San Giorgio, on Italy's Adriatic coast. "Studio" in Italian usage points to a professional-services or design practice, and "SRLS" is the simplified limited-liability form used by small startups, freelancers, and practices because it carries lower minimum capital requirements. The name describes a small office, not a facility that houses servers.

The entry carries no capacity figure, no operator, and no website, and its suitability field is null. The only infrastructure fact attached to it is an airport 36 miles away in Falconara Marittima. Nothing here supports treating it as a data center, and the record itself documents the mistag rather than inventing specifications to fill the gap.

For AI scaling this point is a non-event. It adds no megawatts, no grid load, and no building. It is useful only as a caution about the source layer: OpenStreetMap tags are contributed, not audited, so a telecom=data_center label can attach to a one-person practice. Any count of Italian data centers drawn from this dataset without name-level review will overstate the total, and the error runs in the direction that flatters supply.
